survey.what_is_it: library/engine — Arp, horde's source of generated notes: a C++ note-generation library (the simple arpeggiator for horde 1.0 first; step sequencing and generative MIDI after 1.0) that horde hosts ahead of its engine, plus a browser lab twin for playing and listening. NOT a standalone plugin (Q1).

architecture_rung.earned_by: Note-lifecycle invariants (exactly one terminal per emitted note on every path, a sample-exact grid against the transport, identical output across block sizes and sample rates, seed determinism) give a fresh-context verifier mechanical ground truth. Rung 1 rejected: horde's 1.0 depends on a core only its author would have checked. Rung 3 rejected: one small core, no independent seams, no demonstrated bottleneck.

survey.domain_core_llm_must_not_own: A pure note processor: notes in, notes out, with transport and tempo arriving as data. Held-note set (NoteRef identity, never a bare key), latch/hold, the sustain pedal as input hold, pattern modes, the step grid derived from the transport (never from block boundaries), sample offsets per emitted event, gate length, swing, transposition steps, velocity modes, scale quantize (horde's {root, mask} schema; global read never owned, or Arp's own, D-010), restart rules, and the terminal for every emitted note on every path. Deterministic code only: seeded mulberry32 streams, no wall-clock reads, no allocation/locks/syscalls on the audio thread (buffers sized at prepare), framework-free; UI, host and horde glue are thin adapters. No engine assumed downstream (horde's FX device after 1.0 may run it on MIDI sidechain notes). AI proposes and judges at design time only.

scope_1_0.modes: up, down, up-down (with and without repeated ends), as played, chord, random (seeded mulberry32; same input + seed repeats exactly). Open 1, by poll.
scope_1_0.rate: tempo-synced only, by horde's division names (intake/tempo-divisions.md), stored by name, dotted and triplet included. Free rate in Hz deferred past 1.0. Open 2, by poll.
scope_1_0.controls: transposition steps (the whole pattern repeats, shifted each pass: steps 0-8, step size in semitones or scale degrees, D-014; replaced octaves), gate length, swing, latch/hold, velocity (as played / fixed / accented by step), optional quantize to horde's global scale.
scope_1_0.sustain_pedal: The pedal holds the arp's INPUT: keys released while CC 64 is down stay in the pattern until pedal-up, as if held. Arp consumes CC 64 and does not forward it to the engine, so its own emitted notes never pile up as tails. Composes with latch. Open 3, by poll.
scope_1_0.restart: A PARAMETER with three values: on a new chord from silence (step 1 at the next grid tick); on the bar (step index from song position); free-running. Step TIMING is always the transport grid; restart decides only which step plays next. Each value carries its own invariants. Open 4, by poll (the human chose all three over the single recommended rule).
scope_1_0.morph: ALL Arp settings are morph targets with horde's corners. Continuous settings blend; discrete settings (mode, rate, steps, restart, velocity mode, latch) switch at a threshold — the threshold rule, where a switch lands relative to the grid, and that no switch strands a note without its terminal are Phase A spec items. Open 5, by poll (the human chose all over global).
scope_1_0.presets_undo: Every setting is part of a horde preset and undoable.
scope_1_0.repeats_chord_stage: Added 2026-10-22 by poll (D-018): repeats 0-16 (0 = forever; one repeat = one full cycle of the whole pattern, counted from the gesture); a chord stage before the arp (up to 6 shifts, semitones/degrees, quantizable) with its OWN `chord` stream so horde can route chord and arp to different oscillators (Q-H7). Lock = existing latch replace (no change). The human intends to FREEZE functionality after this batch.
scope_1_0.time_mode_library_step_offset: Added 2026-10-22 by poll (D-016): rate_mode sync|time, step_time_us shown as ms and Hz, firing from the key press; a user-pattern library (UI/adapter; lab/patterns/ + browser; horde presets via Q-H6); per-step `step` x pattern step_size (semitones|degrees) replacing `oct`.
scope_1_0.landed_deferred: D-012's `landed` (order + timing of presses) is DEFERRED past 1.0 by the human (D-014); design preserved in docs/deferred/landed.md.
scope_1_0.chord_modes_user_pattern: Added 2026-10-22 by poll (D-011): four chord + note order styles (chord_walk, stride, chord_between, pairs); a per-step `pick` (order | 1-8 | low | high | chord; only `order` advances the order stream); the user pattern `user` (up to 16 steps, notes and rhythm per step, preset data, set off the audio thread). In 1.0, lab first.
scope_1_0.trigger_output: Added 2026-10-21 by poll (D-007), from horde ADR-267 A1: step patterns carry a trigger lane (0–8); a firing step emits Trigger{lane} at its on-time; trigger-only steps exist; triggers are performance events (no history, no terminal). Lane routing is horde's (Q-H3).
scope_1_0.phase0_additions: Added 2026-10-21 by poll (D-006, Q-A4): latch with two behaviours (replace / append); gate above 100% (legato overlap; a repeated key is a forced terminal at the next step); per-step probability in step patterns (deterministic draw from seed, absolute step, lane); ratchets (2–4 exact sub-steps within a step). Each gets spec rows, invariants with planted controls, and a morph rule.
scope_1_0.pattern_bank: Added 2026-10-21 by poll (D-004). Two kinds of entry: (a) note-ORDER styles beyond the six modes above (converge/diverge, thumb/pinky families, random variants…), and (b) preset STEP patterns (per-step rhythm, rests, ties, accent, gate, octave jump) that play over an order style. 1.0 ships a curated STARTER bank (~12–16 entries) on a data-driven bank format, so the bank grows after 1.0 without core changes. Every entry runs through the same invariant suite. Clean-room: generic algorithms, our own names; screenshots of other arps are inspiration only. Bank selection is a discrete setting, so it morphs per Q-A1.

oracle_shape.goldens: INVARIANTS FIRST, then pinned goldens. Each detector proven with a must-fail (planted) control: every note on gets exactly one terminal on every path (pattern change, held-chord change, switch-off, transport stop/jump/loop, panic, morph switch); the grid is sample-exact against the transport; output identical across block sizes and sample rates; same seed gives the same output; quantize keeps every note in the scale; no allocation on the process path. Per-pattern goldens pinned once the C++ exists, never before (horde ADR-142: parity must not enshrine a defect).
oracle_shape.layer_0: ./verify fast — kit gates (integrity, leak) + structure/manifest sanity from day zero; grows the C++ invariant tests and the lab smoke as they land.
oracle_shape.layer_e: ./verify full — fast + goldens + sweeps; CPU in Release reported, NEVER a gate.
oracle_shape.ci: fast only (Linux runner; public repo, so no minutes budget); full is local.

second_implementation.note: The lab is a listening twin, never a parity target. The C++ core is the reference from day one, judged by its invariants.
